transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thanks. Um… I’m here because I’ve been having a hard time at work around heights, I guess. I’m a construction manager, so it’s not exactly ideal.

Whenever I have to get near a scaffold, a roof edge, or an upper platform, my head just kind of tells me I’m about to go over—even when I can see the rails are there and I know the setup is supposed to be safe. I know that probably sounds a little irrational, but it’s been getting hard to deal with.
When you’re near heights at work, do you ever experience sudden episodes of intense fear or panic, like your heart racing, sweating, or feeling like you can’t breathe?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it does hit pretty fast. Like, the second I step onto temporary stairs or even start walking toward an open upper floor, my chest tightens up, my hands get wet, and I get this feeling like my legs might lock before I can make myself take another step.

I know that probably sounds kind of extreme, but that’s what happens.
